scope: Legacy ordinary exec file capabilities and authorization through the shared conversation execution record
verified: Actual read_file, list_files, search_files, write_file and edit_file calls settle original grants, canonical outcomes and Evidence, with one 16-token ledger row. Rust rejects acquisition while the legacy owner is active and accepts it after a recorded stop.
Two calls received in the same model response both settle before the next request. A read failure after dispatch retains the original grant. A rejected edit prior to dispatch records denial.
On macOS, a real filesystem error after admission leaves the original write grant and stopped owner with an unresolved mutation. Rust rejects recovery and acquisition of that session.

Legacy headless ask inside a real stdin PTY records denial when the approval listener is unavailable. The real TUI Host separately passes allow-once, denial and a late allow racing with stop, with no file effect from the late grant.

initialFailures.observation: TUI typecheck rejected lookup by the public string capability ID in a literal-key Map. The explicit registry type preserves all five manifest-backed entries.
The compiled candidate still returned conversation_execution_out_of_scope because the Store guard allowed only write and edit. The guard was corrected before rebuilding and running the public cases.

limits: The legacy assembly requires the opt-in marker and flag, an explicit file allowlist, chat mode and no Hook configuration. The native executable does not invoke this assembly.
The filesystem permission error case ran on macOS only. The Linux container ran as root.
Synthetic data and loopback provider. The TUI Host cases used its real approval subscriber, without accepting any change to the default CLI, installed processes or user data.
